trials.notes: Chose WP_HTML_Processor, used only documented methods, and followed the documented subtree-text pattern: create_fragment(), next_tag(), record depth, next_token(), require #text, and read get_modifiable_text(). The is_tag_closer() guard is redundant because plain next_tag('H1') skips closers by default, but it is documented and harmless. Passed all 8 cases.

Same high-adherence implementation as trial-1. It uses the structurally aware processor and the depth-bounded token walk described by the docs, accumulates only ordinary text tokens, and relies on documented decoded text semantics. No API misuse or _doing_it_wrong records. Passed all 8 cases.

Matches the canonical documented pattern closely. Correct processor choice, no undocumented calls, idiomatic token walking, correct decoded-text handling, null only when no H1, empty string for no text descendants, and graceful best-effort behavior on an unclosed H1. Passed all 8 cases.

failure_analysis: No hidden case failed in any trial: all three candidates passed all 8 frozen expectations. The docs worked well because the Tag Processor overview explicitly says to use WP_HTML_Processor for collecting element text and walking subtrees, while the HTML Processor's "Recipe: collect DOM-style text from a subtree" directly demonstrates the needed pattern: create a fragment parser, find a container tag, record current depth, walk with next_token(), append only #text tokens, and call get_modifiable_text(). The next_token(), get_current_depth(), and get_modifiable_text() sections also cover the key edge cases: text may be split across tokens, token walks do not stop automatically at an element boundary, get_modifiable_text() is already decoded for #text nodes, unguarded modifiable text is too broad, and read-only extraction may choose its own policy for incomplete input. The only near-miss was that trials 1 and 2 added an unnecessary is_tag_closer() check after next_tag('H1'), suggesting the default opener-only behavior of next_tag() was understood well enough to pass but not fully internalized.

doc_gaps.problem: The docs state in the parameter table that tag closers are skipped by default, but examples elsewhere still include is_tag_closer() checks. This can leave readers unsure whether next_tag('TAG') can return a closer.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a short prose note near the simple string-query examples: plain next_tag('TAG') matches opening tags only; use tag_closers => 'visit' before is_tag_closer() matters.

doc_gaps.problem: The depth-bounded walk contract is documented, but the related guarantees for empty elements, virtual/end-of-input closers, and read-only incomplete-input policy are spread across multiple sections.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Consolidate a compact contract note for subtree scans: record opener depth, continue while depth >= opener depth, append desired token types, the first shallower token is outside the subtree, empty subtrees yield no text tokens, and callers decide whether paused_at_incomplete_token() matters.
